improvement.title: Preserve complete workload setup output before finalizing evidence

failureFirst.reproducer: A setup parent spawned a detached unrefed descendant inheriting stdout/stderr, then exited before the descendant wrote a delayed line.
failureFirst.observedFailure: setup/0.log contained only '[stdout] setup parent exiting' and omitted 'setup late ok'.
failureFirst.rootCause: Workload-pack setup persisted setup logs after child exit even though inherited stdio could still be open and emit additional output.

implementation: Added bounded waitForClose process lifecycle helper without changing existing waitForExit or terminate semantics.
Workload-pack setup now waits for the child close boundary, within the existing setup timeout, before persisting setup logs.
Added a real detached-descendant regression proving late inherited stdout is retained.

ecosystemRotation: property-based testing, model/state-machine testing, coverage-guided fuzzing, stateful API fuzzing, crash minimization and replay

candidates.head: f4b2f3a2f90a0fb08ccfa07b46bb7f1a5a35caec
candidates.purpose: Property-based and model-based testing for TypeScript/JavaScript.
candidates.architecture: Generators/arbitraries plus commands/models, shrinking, seeds and replay paths.
candidates.relevantFerrumCapability: Lifecycle, session, process, restart and race-state verification.
candidates.harvest: Model commands, specialized command shrinking, deterministic seed/path replay.
candidates.integrationMode: isolated dev-only experiment before any dependency decision
candidates.expectedMeasurableBenefit: Find valid lifecycle/interleaving failures and shrink them to minimal deterministic reproductions.
candidates.compatibilityRisks: Unbounded or unseeded randomized tests can add CI time and nondeterminism.
candidates.upstreamIssues: No Ferrum-specific blocker identified in this pass.
candidates.benchmarkOrProductionEvidence: Active mature ecosystem with model-based testing and reproducible seed/path semantics.
candidates.smallestExperiment: Bounded fixed-seed Ferrum process/session lifecycle model with one planted lifecycle defect.
candidates.acceptanceTest: Reproduce the planted defect, shrink to a minimal command sequence, replay exactly by seed/path, stay within a fixed runtime budget.
candidates.nextReviewTrigger: Run 61 lifecycle-model experiment or material upstream API change.

candidates.head: b20881b9a7e44be44903df6d6c1f0f718e0cda19
candidates.purpose: Schema-driven API property and stateful testing.
candidates.architecture: OpenAPI/GraphQL generation with stateful chained requests and shrinking.
candidates.harvest: Fixed-seed stateful API sequences and minimized failing examples.
candidates.integrationMode: subprocess experiment against Ferrum disposable API fixture
candidates.expectedMeasurableBenefit: Discover API state-sequence failures beyond hand-authored requests while retaining minimized replayable cases.
candidates.compatibilityRisks: Additional Python/tool setup and potentially expensive search space.
candidates.benchmarkOrProductionEvidence: Widely used schema-aware API testing project with stateful workflows.
candidates.smallestExperiment: Run a bounded fixed-seed stateful campaign against Ferrum's disposable service fixture.
candidates.acceptanceTest: Real service stays authoritative; any discovered failure is minimized and deterministically replayable with full Ferrum HTTP/process evidence.
candidates.nextReviewTrigger: After fast-check lifecycle experiment or new API coverage need.

candidates.head: e91222467062df2977417fa84827692a2f62ba65
candidates.architecture: Rust/LibAFL sequence corpus, OpenAPI seeds, mutation and constraint solving.
candidates.harvest: Sequence corpus management and coverage-guided selection/mutation.
candidates.expectedMeasurableBenefit: Potentially reach deeper API state combinations than black-box schema generation.
candidates.compatibilityRisks: Heavier integration and runtime cost than Ferrum's native API path.
candidates.upstreamIssues: Complexity must justify itself over Schemathesis on the same fixture.
candidates.smallestExperiment: Same disposable API fixture and time budget as Schemathesis.
candidates.acceptanceTest: Higher useful state/bug coverage within bounded cost, minimized/replayable failure, no loss of Ferrum evidence.
candidates.nextReviewTrigger: Only if Schemathesis leaves demonstrated coverage gaps.

candidates.head: 4c14e1bf63d82475ea057d6208e6f2eac87fa680
candidates.architecture: In-process Node fuzz targets with corpus management and replay.
candidates.harvest: Coverage-guided corpus and crash replay for isolated pure functions.
candidates.integrationMode: isolated parser fuzz target only when a parser-specific gap is observed
candidates.expectedMeasurableBenefit: Increase edge-case coverage for pure input processors without exercising full runtimes.
candidates.compatibilityRisks: Native tooling and fuzz runtime are disproportionate for general lifecycle testing.
candidates.upstreamIssues: Not suited as the primary cross-platform Ferrum lifecycle harness.
candidates.benchmarkOrProductionEvidence: Mature coverage-guided fuzzing approach for JavaScript.
candidates.smallestExperiment: Fuzz one pure Ferrum parser with a planted edge defect and retained corpus.
candidates.acceptanceTest: Find/replay the defect with bounded runtime and no persistent dependency unless the value is material.
candidates.nextReviewTrigger: A concrete parser/redaction defect or Linux-only fuzzing lane.

candidates.head: 6d984deedbc54aad957fa3da0c7e9e5df23a2aee
candidates.purpose: Stateful REST API fuzzing with producer-consumer dependencies.
candidates.architecture: API grammar inference, dependency-aware sequences, bug buckets and replay.
candidates.harvest: Producer-consumer dependency modeling and replayable bug buckets.
candidates.expectedMeasurableBenefit: Generate semantically valid request sequences that hand-authored or independent requests miss.
candidates.compatibilityRisks: Heavy workflow compared with Ferrum's current native HTTP actions.
candidates.upstreamIssues: No direct Ferrum integration planned until a dependency-rich API fixture exists.
candidates.benchmarkOrProductionEvidence: Microsoft stateful REST fuzzing research and implementation.
candidates.smallestExperiment: Dependency-rich disposable API fixture with a fixed seed and replay.
candidates.acceptanceTest: Discover a dependency-order defect and replay it deterministically with Ferrum evidence attached.
candidates.nextReviewTrigger: A Ferrum workload with nontrivial producer-consumer API dependencies.

candidates.head: 0951a8c09792f30a083c49b366abcb0af6edcf60
candidates.purpose: Automated test generation and fuzzing for APIs.
candidates.architecture: Search-based and schema-aware generation with white/black-box modes.
candidates.harvest: Search-based sequence optimization and generated-test evaluation ideas.
candidates.expectedMeasurableBenefit: Compare whether heavier search produces materially stronger API fault discovery.
candidates.upstreamIssues: Too heavy for default Ferrum without clear coverage advantage.
candidates.benchmarkOrProductionEvidence: Active research project with industrial/API evaluation work.
candidates.smallestExperiment: Same disposable API fixture and fixed time budget as lighter candidates.
candidates.acceptanceTest: Materially higher useful fault discovery with reproducible artifacts and acceptable setup cost.
candidates.nextReviewTrigger: Only after lighter API fuzzers establish a measurable ceiling.

candidates.head: 41004301f02bcb35b7953518ed16705c4cf0211c
candidates.purpose: Property-based and stateful testing for Python.
candidates.architecture: Strategies, state machines, shrinking, example database and replay.
candidates.harvest: Ghost/model state separation, shrinking and durable failing examples.
candidates.expectedMeasurableBenefit: Improve Ferrum-native model-testing design quality without adding a Python dependency.
candidates.compatibilityRisks: Direct adoption would create an unnecessary second-language test harness for Node-native code.
candidates.upstreamIssues: No direct Ferrum blocker; dependency mismatch drives transplant-only decision.
candidates.benchmarkOrProductionEvidence: Mature widely deployed property-based testing framework.
candidates.smallestExperiment: Compare its state-machine/shrink concepts against fast-check command models for Ferrum lifecycle cases.
candidates.acceptanceTest: Ferrum-native model retains deterministic replay/minimization without Python runtime dependency.
candidates.nextReviewTrigger: If fast-check command modeling cannot express required lifecycle invariants.

candidates.head: 4fc61fbdf5f0c262d2c39309e3b5ca6a35349740
candidates.purpose: Continuous production fuzzing service and corpus infrastructure.
candidates.architecture: Fuzz engines, corpora, minimization, crash triage and continuous infrastructure.
candidates.relevantFerrumCapability: Fuzz corpus/minimization/replay architecture and future continuous fuzz lane.
candidates.harvest: Corpus retention, minimized crash artifacts, reproducible fuzz environment identity.
candidates.expectedMeasurableBenefit: Higher-quality durable fuzz evidence and replay if Ferrum later adds continuous fuzzing.
candidates.compatibilityRisks: Far too heavy for ordinary Ferrum CI or cross-platform product paths.
candidates.upstreamIssues: Service model does not match Ferrum's normal local agent tester execution.
candidates.smallestExperiment: Borrow only corpus/minimized-crash manifest ideas for a local bounded fuzz experiment.
candidates.acceptanceTest: Useful failure minimization/replay without introducing service dependence.
candidates.nextReviewTrigger: If local fuzz experiments prove enough value to justify a continuous lane.

candidates.head: 52ecc61cb587ee99c26825a112a21abf19c7448c
candidates.purpose: CI-integrated fuzzing for pull requests and continuous builds.
candidates.relevantFerrumCapability: Future bounded PR fuzzing lane and crash-artifact retention.
candidates.harvest: PR fuzzing workflow patterns, testcase download and corpus identity.
candidates.expectedMeasurableBenefit: Run narrow fuzz checks on changed parsers without converting normal Ferrum CI into a fuzz service.
candidates.compatibilityRisks: Language/runtime support and setup cost must be proven for Ferrum's Node use cases.
candidates.upstreamIssues: Not the first choice while fast-check/Jazzer experiments are smaller and closer to Ferrum.
candidates.smallestExperiment: Only after a successful local fuzz target exists, compare PR integration overhead.
candidates.acceptanceTest: Same fuzz target, equivalent or stronger findings, acceptable CI overhead and deterministic crash retrieval.
candidates.nextReviewTrigger: After a local coverage-guided Ferrum target is proven.

candidates.head: 7fab097d98cf88a7c7534a55e2209534c7afaa77
candidates.architecture: FuzzIL intermediate representation, program generation/mutation, engine instrumentation and corpus evolution.
candidates.relevantFerrumCapability: Only general corpus/minimization architecture ideas; target mismatch for app testing.
candidates.harvest: Structured intermediate representation and corpus evolution concepts.
candidates.integrationMode: reject direct integration; research reference only
candidates.expectedMeasurableBenefit: None for ordinary Ferrum application/runtime verification without a JS-engine testing requirement.
candidates.compatibilityRisks: Targets JavaScript engines rather than Ferrum workflows, browsers-as-apps, APIs or process lifecycle.
candidates.upstreamIssues: Fundamental scope mismatch for Ferrum's general application tester direction.
candidates.benchmarkOrProductionEvidence: Project Zero JavaScript engine fuzzer used for engine security research.
candidates.acceptanceTest: Reconsider only if Ferrum gains an explicit JavaScript-engine fuzzing requirement.
candidates.nextReviewTrigger: A new explicit JS-engine testing requirement, not ordinary ecosystem rotation.

independentChallenge.reason: The deterministic real-process reproducer fully explained the setup-evidence defect. Adding a fuzz/property dependency in the same patch would add toolchain churn and obscure the narrow root cause.
independentChallenge.nextExperiment: Run an isolated fast-check model/state-machine lifecycle experiment, then a Schemathesis stateful API experiment against the existing disposable real service fixture.

guardrails: No reduced evidence, diagnostics, media fidelity, item counts, refresh frequency or validation strength.
No viewport-only, capped, synthetic-only or stale-cache shortcut.
Randomized/property tests must be bounded, seeded, replayable and additive to real-runtime acceptance.
New fuzzing dependencies remain isolated experiments until identical-workload evidence proves material value.
nextCursor: bounded fast-check lifecycle/state-machine model with deterministic seed/path shrink+replay
Schemathesis stateful API differential against existing disposable real service fixture
WuppieFuzz only if the lighter API experiment leaves a demonstrated coverage gap
Jazzer.js only for a concrete pure parser/redaction fuzzing gap
